correctness.rationale: At every unit vector, two nonzero quadratic-form values have angular separation at most delta. The exact identity 1+r^2+2r cos(delta)=(r+cos(delta))^2+sin^2(delta) proves the two regimes and their boundary; transposition and supremum transfer to ordinary numerical radius for all bounded operators without any assumption of norm attainment. One-dimensional sector-edge scalars saturate the obtuse case and positive perturbations approach the acute infimum. Strict finite-dimensional endpoint and nonstrict infinite-dimensional counterexample were checked. The embedded standard-library checker verifies the critical algebra and rational witness from its own package path.

value.rationale: Determines the exact optimal lower numerical-radius sum constant left unsharp by the direct 2020/2026 theorems; it quantifies when sectoriality preserves positivity-like monotonicity and when the best factor must drop, with an exact pi/4 common-angle transition. The two-angle classification is dimension-free and scalar-sharp, so its relevance is not to an arbitrary parameter slice. The nontrivial improvement reaches factor 1 in the acute region and sin(2 gamma), much larger than cos^2 gamma, elsewhere.
